deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: No upstream signature was removed or reordered, so vllm-ascend code does not need a hard compatibility edit. Required work: (1) Audit every Ascend multimodal processor/dummy builder that inherits BaseProcessingInfo/BaseMultiModalProcessor or consumes MultiModalConfig dummy options. None currently read BaseDummyOptions.count or VideoDummyOptions.count directly (grep confirms only itertools.count), but keep that invariant: count is now Optional and VideoDummyOptions.count defaults to None, so any new code must use `overrides.count or 999` (as minicpmv now does), and tests/mocks that build MultiModalConfig or limit_per_prompt must accept count=None. (2) Qwen3-VL-derived Ascend models now default to 32 videos per prompt (Qwen3.5/VL-MoE, D3, ClefFlash, Qwen4Exp) and enforce VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_PREPROCESSING_BYTES; update Ascend e2e/UT expectations and docs that assumed 999 videos, and document that operators can override with --limit-mm-per-prompt.video. (3) Ascend's custom GLM5Next path is not covered by the new checks because it reimplements video/image preprocessing in vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/processor.py. To preserve the upstream DoS bound, Glm5NextVideoProcessor._preprocess (and Glm5NextImageProcessor._preprocess) or Glm5NextMultiModalProcessor._apply_hf_processor_main should estimate frame count after sample_frames, resolved size, dtype and accumulated output bytes, then call vllm.multimodal.processing.context.validate_video_preprocessing_budget / estimate_video_pixel_element_size / get_video_frame_dimensions (or image_budget.validate_image_tensor_budget for images), skipping when is_profiling_media() is set. (4) The Ascend Qwen3.5 device-side image path (AscendQwen2VLImageProcessor._preprocess, _AscendVLPreprocessMixin) already bypasses HF image preprocessing; this commit does not add an image budget for Qwen3VL, so no regression, but if parity is desired add validate_image_tensor_budget when the raw-pixel fast path is taken. (5) Verify profiling/dummy generation still works: BaseMultiModalProcessor now wraps apply() in profiling_media(), so Ascend profiling should not hit the new limits.
deep_analysis.risk: Low operational risk to existing Ascend functionality: the changes are additive/backwards-compatible, NPU platform/worker/attention/kernel paths are untouched, and the new budget lives entirely in CPU-side multimodal processing. The main risks are behavioral rather than structural: (a) Qwen3.5-VL/D3/ClefFlash/Qwen4Exp silently drop the default video-per-prompt cap from 999 to 32, and large video/image requests that previously succeeded may now raise VLLMValidationError from VLLM_MAX_MEDIA_PREPROCESSING_BYTES, so Ascend e2e tests and user workloads must be checked; (b) GLM5Next and any other Ascend-custom preprocessing path remains unbounded, so the security fix is incomplete for those models on NPU (parity gap, not a regression); (c) VideoDummyOptions.count/BaseDummyOptions.count becoming Optional can cause arithmetic/type errors only if Ascend code starts reading .count as an int, which no current code does. No impact expected on ACL graph capture, KV cache, scheduler, communicator, or attention backends.

Do the same in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/fused_gdn_gating.py::fused_gdn_gating_patch`, `vllm_ascend/device/device_op.py::DeviceOperator.fla_gdn_prefill` (A5 chunk32 currently passes raw b with `allow_neg_eigval=False`), `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/gdn/gdn_recoverssm_verify.py`, and the 310P `fused_gdn_gating_pytorch`/`AscendGatedDeltaNetAttention310._forward_core` path. deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
This commit is a global rename of the engine stats flag `log_stats` -> `collect_stats` plus a behavior change (stats are now collected when an OTLP tracing endpoint is set even if `disable_log_stats=True`).

1) vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py (highest priority): `BalanceScheduler` is installed unconditionally by `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py` as `_sched_mod.Scheduler = BalanceScheduler`, and `SchedulerConfig.get_scheduler_cls()` re-imports that module attribute, so on the next vLLM main bump EngineCore will call `BalanceScheduler(..., collect_stats=...)`. Its explicit `__init__` only accepts `log_stats`, causing `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'collect_stats'` at startup for the default scheduler path. Make the signature/forwarding version-compatible (accept `collect_stats` on new vLLM, keep `log_stats` for 0.34.0 and forward the correct keyword to `super().__init__`). Rename `self.log_stats` in the `not vllm_version_is('0.34.0')` branch (~L191) to `self.collect_stats`; the unguarded reference in `schedule` (~L746) must work on both lanes (version-gated helper or getattr fallback); leave the `if vllm_version_is('0.34.0')` block (~L862) on `log_stats`.

2) vllm_ascend/core/recompute_scheduler.py: rename `self.log_stats` to `self.collect_stats` inside the `not vllm_version_is('0.34.0')` guard (~L225); make the unguarded schedule reference (~L863) lane-compatible; keep `self.log_stats` in the `if vllm_version_is('0.34.0')` block (~L990).

3) vllm_ascend/core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py: rename `self.log_stats` to `self.collect_stats` in the main-lane guard (~L425); rename/guard `self.kv_cache_manager.log_stats` (~L327, KVCacheManager attribute also renamed) and the unguarded references (~L381 `_lb_pause_request`, ~L1045 scheduling, ~L1171) with a version-compatible accessor; keep `self.log_stats` under the 0.34.0 branch.

4) Update unit tests that instantiate schedulers: tests/ut/core/test_recompute_scheduler_short_request_first.py (~L121), tests/ut/core/test_dyntra_lb_scheduler.py (~L110), tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py (~L769), tests/ut/kv_offload/utils.py (~L169) — switch `log_stats=True` to `collect_stats=True` for the new-vLLM lane (or route through a small helper that picks the right keyword by `vllm_version_is`). Leave EPLB `_should_record_current_step(log_stats=...)` usages untouched; they are a different Ascend/EPLB API.

5) No change needed for BaseEngineCore/EngineCoreClient/OutputProcessor subclasses (Ascend does not subclass them), but verify the new OTLP behavior: with tracing enabled, upstream will now collect IterationStats/SchedulerStats/prefix-cache stats even when `--disable-log-stats` is passed, so Ascend custom schedulers must record events keyed on `collect_stats` (not `log_stats`) to stay consistent.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. The rename itself is mechanical, but `BalanceScheduler` is the unconditional default Scheduler replacement for NPU, so a missed signature update becomes a hard `TypeError` at engine startup for all default deployments, and missed attribute references become `AttributeError` in schedule/preempt/stat-collection paths when stats or tracing is enabled. The dual-lane `vllm_version_is('0.34.0')` guards mean the fix must keep 0.34.0 (`log_stats`) and main (`collect_stats`) both working; unit tests in tests/ut give good coverage to catch regressions.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: Update vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py::AscendMoERunner.apply_routed_output_transform (line ~437) to accept the new optional argument `residual: torch.Tensor | None = None` and forward it to the base implementation, e.g. `super().apply_routed_output_transform(fused_output, residual=residual)`, while keeping the existing Ascend SP-overlap `wait_for_output()` handling. Then mirror the new upstream combine semantics in AscendMoERunner.forward (line ~279): when `shared_output is not None` and `getattr(self.routed_output_transform, "accumulates_residual", False)` is true, call `apply_routed_output_transform(fused_output, residual=shared_output)` and use its return directly (do not also run the `torch._foreach_add([shared_output], [fused_output])` combine); otherwise retain the existing one-argument transform call followed by the NPU `_foreach_add` combine. This matches the new `LatentUpProjection.accumulates_residual` protocol added in vllm/models/hy_v4_flash/nvidia/moe.py. Add a unit test in tests/ut/ops/test_fused_moe.py covering a transform with `accumulates_residual=True` and the `residual=` keyword, and verify the existing one-argument SP-overlap tests still pass.
deep_analysis.risk: Low. The behavioral change only activates when a routed output transform sets `accumulates_residual=True` (currently only HY4 Flash's LatentUpProjection, which is not Ascend-supported), so default `residual=None` preserves current Kimi K3/DeepSeek latent-MoE behavior. The main risk is leaving Ascend's copied forward in the old one-arg/`_foreach_add` form: any future NPU model using an accumulating transform would silently double-add the shared output or skip the fused accumulate GEMM. The change also must not disturb the Ascend SP shared-expert overlap (`wait_for_output`) or the `torch._foreach_add` fast path used for ordinary MoE combines.
